text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers:
- The government said its goal was to increase the number of tourist overnight stays to nine million from the current 5.8 million in the next five years.
- Slovenia and Croatia signed a social agreement in Zagreb on Thursday. The agreement determines rights of Slovenians and Croatians who are or were employed in the neighbouring country.
- Slovenian basketball team Smelt Olimpija lost the first EuroLeague quarter-final game with Italian Stefanel by 90 against 94. The second match will be in Ljubljana on Tuesday.

- Management of petrol trader Petrol said it planned to pay a dividend of 700 tolars in the first half ot the year. The management's proposal has to be approved at the shareholders' meeting on April 4.

- The state Inspection Office said it would increase control on whether restaurants follow new non-smoking regulations from May 18, six months after the enforcement of the new tobacco law which restricted tobacco advertising and use of tobacco products.

- Slovenian investment legislation should be changed in line with European Union rules in order for the country to be able to attract more foreign investors, Matej Kovac, head of the state's Trade and Investment Promotion Office, said.
- Car insurance companies said they would prepare a new insurance premium system in the next two months where payments would depend upon the driver's sex, age, driving experience and driving history.

- The state's Bank Rehabilitation Agency said the two state-owned banks Nova Ljubljanska Banka and Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor would reduce basic borrowing interest rates to seven percent from 8.5 in line with the general decrease of bank interest rates in the country.
